Electric Vehicle Range Analysis

Does drivetrain configuration moderate the battery–range relationship?

Mahour Rezvani, Markus Rosario, Desiree Ng, Doa Binte Rashid — UBC STAT 306

2026-11-16

Reproducible report. Every number and figure below is computed at render time from the raw dataset (data/raw/). The original coursework estimates are preserved exactly; this report adds an explicit robustness analysis that qualifies how strongly the drivetrain interaction can be claimed.

1 Research question

As electric vehicles (EVs) become central to low-emission transport, range anxiety remains a key consumer concern. Battery capacity is the most direct driver of range, but drivetrain configuration may also matter: all-wheel-drive (AWD) vehicles are heavier and mechanically more complex than two-wheel-drive (2WD) vehicles, so they may convert stored energy into distance less efficiently.

Does drivetrain (AWD vs. 2WD) moderate the association between battery capacity and driving range, after controlling for vehicle length?

Vehicle length is a control / proxy for mass (weight is not in the dataset) and a plausible confounder — associated with both battery capacity and range.

2 Data

The Electric Vehicle Specs Dataset (2025) (Urvish Ahir, Kaggle; scraped from ev-database.org; CC BY 4.0) covers 478 2025 EV models. We use range_km (response), battery_capacity_kWh (predictor), drivetrain (AWD vs. 2WD = FWD+RWD), and length_mm (control).

raw <- read.csv(RAW_DATA, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

ev <- raw |>
  transmute(
    range_km, battery_capacity_kWh, length_mm,
    drivetrain        = factor(drivetrain, levels = c("FWD", "RWD", "AWD")),
    drivetrain_binary = factor(ifelse(drivetrain == "AWD", "AWD", "2WD"),
                               levels = c("2WD", "AWD"))
  )

# Validation: no missing analysis values, all positive before log transforms.
stopifnot(nrow(ev) == 478, !anyNA(ev))
assert_positive(ev, c("range_km", "battery_capacity_kWh", "length_mm"))

ev <- ev |>
  mutate(log_range   = log(range_km),
         log_battery = log(battery_capacity_kWh),
         log_length  = log(length_mm))

c(n = nrow(ev), `2WD` = sum(ev$drivetrain_binary == "2WD"),
  AWD = sum(ev$drivetrain_binary == "AWD"))
##   n 2WD AWD 
## 478 287 191

2.1 Summary statistics by drivetrain

ev |>
  group_by(Drivetrain = drivetrain_binary) |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            `Mean range (km)`   = round(mean(range_km), 1),
            `Mean battery (kWh)` = round(mean(battery_capacity_kWh), 1),
            `Mean length (mm)`  = round(mean(length_mm), 0), .groups = "drop") |>
  kable(caption = "AWD vehicles have larger batteries, longer bodies, and longer range.")
AWD vehicles have larger batteries, longer bodies, and longer range.
Drivetrain n Mean range (km) Mean battery (kWh) Mean length (mm)
2WD 287 352.9 64.4 4569

3 Exploratory data analysis

The battery–range slope looks steeper for 2WD than AWD — the visual motivation for an interaction term. (The report also notes this is before controlling for length, so it is exploratory, not conclusive.)

ggplot(ev, aes(battery_capacity_kWh, range_km, color = drivetrain_binary)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, formula = y ~ x) +
  labs(title = "Driving range vs battery capacity, by drivetrain",
       x = "Battery capacity (kWh)", y = "Driving range (km)",
       color = "Drivetrain") +
  theme_minimal()

4 Model

Continuous variables are log-transformed (physical reasoning: mass ∝ length, range ∝ battery / length), so coefficients read as elasticities and the interaction is additive on the log scale.

\[\log(\text{range}) = \beta_0 + \beta_1\log(\text{battery}) + \beta_2\,\text{AWD} + \beta_3\log(\text{battery})\cdot\text{AWD} + \beta_4\log(\text{length}) + \varepsilon\]

reg_log <- lm(log_range ~ log_battery * drivetrain_binary + log_length, data = ev)
s <- summary(reg_log)
kable(round(s$coefficients, 4), caption = "Fitted coefficients (OLS).")
Fitted coefficients (OLS).
Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)
(Intercept) 10.9325 0.7251 15.0765 0.0000
log_battery 1.1153 0.0293 38.0942 0.0000
drivetrain_binaryAWD 0.5017 0.2593 1.9347 0.0536
log_length -1.1526 0.0945 -12.2003 0.0000
log_battery:drivetrain_binaryAWD -0.1201 0.0586 -2.0499 0.0409 
data.frame(
  Statistic = c("Multiple R-squared", "Adjusted R-squared",
                "Interaction coef (beta3)", "Interaction p-value (OLS)"),
  Value = c(round(s$r.squared, 4), round(s$adj.r.squared, 4),
            round(coef(reg_log)["log_battery:drivetrain_binaryAWD"], 4),
            round(s$coefficients["log_battery:drivetrain_binaryAWD", "Pr(>|t|)"], 4))
) |> kable(caption = "Model fit and the interaction term under investigation.")
Model fit and the interaction term under investigation.
Statistic Value
Multiple R-squared 0.8452
Adjusted R-squared 0.8439
Interaction coef (beta3) -0.1201
Interaction p-value (OLS) 0.0409

Reading the model. Battery capacity (+1.12 per log-unit, p < 10⁻¹⁴⁰) and length (-1.15, p < 10⁻²⁰) are strong, highly significant predictors; together the model explains ≈ 84% of the variance in log range. The length coefficient is negative after controlling for battery (it is positive unadjusted) — a classic confounding reversal: once battery is held fixed, extra length reflects added mass and energy use.

5 Diagnostics

par(mfrow = c(2, 2)); plot(reg_log); par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

kable(round(car::vif(reg_log, type = "predictor")[, 1:3], 3),
      caption = "Generalized VIF — no multicollinearity concern (all ≈ 2.1).")
Generalized VIF — no multicollinearity concern (all ≈ 2.1).
GVIF Df GVIF^(1/(2*Df))
log_battery 2.114 3 1.133
drivetrain_binary 2.114 3 1.133
log_length 2.114 1 1.454

The residuals-vs-fitted and scale-location plots show mild non-constant variance, and Cook’s distance flags one clearly influential vehicle. These two facts are the reason for the robustness analysis below.

6 Robustness of the interaction

The OLS interaction p-value (0.041) is just below 0.05. Given the diagnostics, we re-estimate it four ways. The main effects stay highly significant in every scenario; the interaction does not.

ix <- "log_battery:drivetrain_binaryAWD"

# 1. HC3 heteroskedasticity-consistent standard errors
V   <- car::hccm(reg_log, type = "hc3")
se  <- sqrt(diag(V)); p_hc3 <- 2 * pt(-abs(coef(reg_log) / se), df.residual(reg_log))

# 2 & 3. Influence refits
cooks  <- cooks.distance(reg_log); n <- nrow(ev)
m_no1  <- lm(formula(reg_log), data = ev[-which.max(cooks), ])
drop_k <- which(cooks > 4 / n)
m_nok  <- lm(formula(reg_log), data = ev[-drop_k, ])

# 4. Three-level drivetrain interaction
m_3    <- lm(log_range ~ log_battery * drivetrain + log_length, data = ev)
p_3    <- car::Anova(m_3, type = 2)["log_battery:drivetrain", "Pr(>F)"]

pval <- function(m) summary(m)$coefficients[ix, "Pr(>|t|)"]
robust <- data.frame(
  Scenario = c("OLS (as reported)", "HC3 robust SE",
               "Drop most influential vehicle",
               sprintf("Drop Cook's D > 4/n (%d pts)", length(drop_k)),
               "Three-level FWD/RWD/AWD interaction"),
  `Interaction p` = round(c(pval(reg_log), p_hc3[ix], pval(m_no1), pval(m_nok), p_3), 3),
  `Sig. at 0.05`  = c("yes", "no", "no", "yes", "no"),
  check.names = FALSE
)
kable(robust, caption = "Sensitivity of the battery × drivetrain interaction.")
Sensitivity of the battery × drivetrain interaction.
Scenario Interaction p Sig. at 0.05
OLS (as reported) 0.041 yes
HC3 robust SE 0.057 no
Drop most influential vehicle 0.146 no
Drop Cook’s D > 4/n (29 pts) 0.005 yes
Three-level FWD/RWD/AWD interaction 0.312 no 
pd <- robust; pd$Scenario <- factor(pd$Scenario, levels = rev(pd$Scenario))
ggplot(pd, aes(`Interaction p`, Scenario, fill = `Interaction p` < 0.05)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.05, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#4C9F70", `FALSE` = "#C0504D"), guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Interaction significance is fragile",
       subtitle = "Dashed line = 0.05", x = "Interaction p-value", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()

Interpretation. The interaction’s sign is stable (2WD has the steeper battery slope) but its significance is fragile: it disappears under robust standard errors, after removing a single influential vehicle, and when drivetrain is not collapsed to binary. It is therefore suggestive, not established.

7 Conclusion & limitations

  • Robust finding: battery capacity and vehicle length are strong predictors of EV driving range on the log scale (adjusted R² ≈ 0.84).
  • Suggestive finding: drivetrain may moderate the battery–range slope (2WD slightly steeper), but the evidence is not statistically robust.
  • Not causal. This is a cross-sectional, observational dataset; results are associations, not causal effects.

Limitations: the dataset does not state the range testing standard (WLTP/EPA/ CLTC); weight is unavailable (length is a proxy); collapsing FWD+RWD into 2WD hides real differences; and the interaction depends on influential-point handling.
